claim.value: Simulation cannot establish the magnitude of an effect in live purchasing.
claim.scope: Quantitative generalization from simulation to live operations; the mapping does not deny every possible evidentiary contribution from simulation.

provenance.rationale: P029 explicitly states the limitation on establishing live-effect magnitude from simulation.

signal_basis.value: Alternate clear and unclear attachment responsibility across comparable fictitious tasks; observe missing attachments recur under ambiguity and improve when clarity returns.
signal_basis.scope: Safe simulation without weakening live controls; the observed recurrence and improvement provide a simulation-specific signal.

provenance.rationale: These spans specify the simulated intervention, comparable fictitious tasks, safety boundary and resulting simulation-specific signal.
The claim is supported within its stated bounds; no conditional empirical warrant is required.

rationale: Even assuming successful execution and the described signal, recurrence and improvement in fictitious tasks do not determine the size of the effect in live purchasing. The mapping supplies no quantitative connection establishing that transfer. This licenses the stated limitation while preserving simulation's possible evidentiary contribution.
uncertainty: No material uncertainty about this bounded limitation; the live-effect magnitude remains unestablished by the simulated signal.
